bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: ALMM-III wafer rollout delays; silver price volatility; forex exposure (hedged at 30-70%); export market tariff wars (US UFLPA compliance); delayed DCR tender awards; cell supply chain disruption from Southeast Asia; execution risk on 12GW cell ramp-up
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and forward-looking; emphasized integration, execution reliability, and long-term resilience over short-term cycles; acknowledged near-term cost pressures but framed them as industry-corrective; tone on policy (RCO, ALMM) was highly positive; no signs of demand slowdown
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 88% of order book has cell cost pass-through — a rare structural advantage in a price-sensitive market; 100% TOPCon capacity (no PERC) signals irreversible tech shift; BESS plan includes integrated cell production — not just pack assembly — indicating deep vertical ambition; export strategy bypasses Indian cells due to reciprocal tariffs, using Southeast Asia as a compliant hub — a hidden global supply chain play
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Backward/vertical integration strategy (module -> cell -> wafer-ingot) aimed at improving supply security, cost competitiveness and reduced reliance on external supply chains
- Established brand and bankability track record: BloombergNEF Tier-1 manufacturer and 8-time KIWA PVEL Reliability Scorecard Top Performer
- Extensive pan-India distribution network of 110 distributors and 550+ dealers across 22 states and 2 Union Territories
- Global footprint with modules supplied to 39+ countries and cumulative shipments crossing 10.46 GW since inception
- Strong order book of 8.2 GW as of 31 March 2026 across diversified customer segments (IPP, Government, C&I, EPC), supporting revenue visibility
- Two decades of manufacturing experience, equipment sourced from the USA, Germany, Switzerland, Japan and China
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw Material Risk — Fluctuations in prices of key inputs such as solar cells, wafers and other materials may impact cost structures and profitability; dependence on imported upstream components may also expose the Company to supply disruptions.
- Diversification Risk — A significant share of revenue is derived from solar module manufacturing, so any slowdown in this segment may impact overall business performance.
- Customer Concentration Risk — Dependence on a limited number of customers may expose the Company to risks related to order concentration or loss of key relationships.
- Competition Risk — Increasing domestic capacity additions and the presence of global players may lead to pricing pressure and margin compression.
- Regulatory and Policy Risk — Changes in government policies, including import duties, localisation requirements and renewable energy regulations, may impact demand, costs and market access.
- Execution Risk — Large-scale expansion and backward integration plans may face risks related to project delays, cost overruns or implementation challenges.
- Technology Transition Risk — Rapid evolution in solar technologies may impact product competitiveness if technology upgrades are delayed.
- Structural Domestic Overcapacity / Global Trade Risk — Domestic module manufacturing capacity is being added faster than near-term demand, creating supply-side imbalance and continued pricing pressure; separately, anti-dumping and countervailing duties imposed by the US on Indian solar cells and modules, along with evolving trade/incentive policies in key export markets, could affect export opportunities, pricing realisations and competitive positioning.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Four stated "proven capabilities": Technology Leadership ("N-Type TOPCon modules with R&D on-going for future technology"), Smart & Automated Operations ("AI-enabled factories"), "Single-Site Integration Edge at Gangaikondan", and Long-Term Value Creation ("Wafer-to-module margin retained in-house, insulating from price cycles").
- The FY30 value-creation thesis is stated as "Higher gross margins | ALMM-aligned non-China supply chain | Upstream value capture | BESS growth engine".
- External bankability validation is a positioning plank: "Bloomberg NEF Tier-1 — 9th consecutive quarter in the bankability test" and "KIWA PVEL Top Performer — 9th time on the Reliability Scorecard".
- Capacity history per the deck's own timeline: 500 MW (2015), 1 GW (2017), 2.5 GW (2021), 3.5 GW (2023), 4.5 GW (2024), 9.5 GW (2025) and 15.5 GW (2026).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Credit rating] "IND A+ (Stable) long-term and IND A1+ short-term credit ratings".
- [Listing] The capacity timeline records "Listed on Stock Exchanges — BSE & NSE" in 2025.
- [Industry/Policy] Third-party industry framing: India power demand CAGR of 7.3% ("fastest major economy"), per-capita 1,460 kWh ("~half global average"), and power demand driving a ₹50 trillion investment across generation, transmission, distribution and renewables.
- [Industry/Policy] ALMM mandates across modules and cells are cited as accelerating domestic manufacturing; PM Surya Ghar and PM-Surya Sarovar Yojana are cited as opening rooftop and floating-solar demand.
- [Storage market] Industry estimates quoted: 321 GWh expected BESS market in India by FY35, 40+ GWh planned via VGF across two tranches, and ₹18,000 cr of PLI I & II for battery manufacturing.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Board-approved phased capital expenditure programme to strengthen upstream integration into cells, wafers and ingots, aligned with evolving regulatory developments such as the proposed ALMM List-III framework, alongside planned expansion of module manufacturing capacity from 9.5 GW to 15.5 GW
- Financial strategy anchored in disciplined execution, prudent capital allocation and long-term value creation, with capex undertaken in a calibrated manner while keeping financial guardrails such as ICR, DSCR and debt-equity ratios within permissible limits
- Phased backward integration strategy into cell manufacturing (N-type first platform) to strengthen control across the value chain and build long-term competitiveness
- Technology roadmap structured around phase gates: TOPCon as the base platform for India-ready deployment, TOPCon+ as an efficiency upgrade pathway, XBC as a future high-efficiency/niche layer, with planned upstream integration into ingot and wafer manufacturing
- Development of a fully integrated manufacturing campus at Gangaikondan, Tamil Nadu incorporating module, cell, wafer and ingot stages
- Multi-technology module portfolio (N-Type, P-Type Mono-PERC, Bifacial, HJT, large-format G12/G12R wafer platforms, half-cut cell architecture) aligned to evolving demand across utility-scale, commercial, industrial and rooftop segments
- Front-loaded regulatory approvals and structured OEM support built into the expansion roadmap to minimise execution delays and ensure smooth capacity stabilisation
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26, Vikram Solar commissioned its 5 GW Vallam facility in Tamil Nadu, taking total operational module manufacturing capacity to 9.5 GW across facilities in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu (Falta, Oragadam and Vallam). The Company is now executing an integrated manufacturing expansion plan centred on a 6 GW solar module manufacturing unit and an associated cell manufacturing facility at Gangaikondan, Tamil Nadu, targeted for commissioning in FY 2026-27, envisaged as a fully integrated campus incorporating module, cell, wafer and ingot stages. Beyond this, the Board has approved a phased capex programme for backward integration into cells, wafers and ingots: a Cell Plant-1 of 9 GW capacity by FY27 (75% backward integration), a Cell Plant-2 adding 3 GW by FY28 (~90% backward integration), and a 12 GW wafer-ingot facility to be commissioned in two 6 GW phases (Phase I by FY29, Phase II by FY30), alongside planned overall module manufacturing capacity expansion from 9.5 GW to 15.5 GW. The Company has also entered the Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) segment through its VION brand (via VSL PowerHive), with a planned 15 GWh BESS capacity by FY30.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic demand continues to grow steadily, supported by policy frameworks and increasing adoption of high-efficiency technologies
- Strong sector tailwinds from India's energy transition: total installed power capacity has surpassed 500 GW with more than half from non-fossil sources; India ranks 3rd globally in installed solar capacity
- Large and diversified project pipeline (90.04 GW solar, ~19.0 GW hybrid projects) supports demand visibility for capacity addition in coming years
- Regulatory tailwinds favour ALMM-compliant, domestically integrated manufacturers: ALMM framework for modules, extension of ALMM to solar cells (List-II), the PLI scheme for high-efficiency modules, and Basic Customs Duty on imported solar cells/modules strengthening domestic manufacturing
- Policy-led demand expansion across applications: PM Surya Ghar rooftop scheme, PM-KUSUM agricultural solar deployment, growing rollout of hybrid/round-the-clock renewable projects, and policy push towards green hydrogen creating additional long-term solar demand
- Credit rating upgrade during the year reflects the robustness of the Company's financial profile, prudent capital management and strong governance practices
- Global renewable energy investment and generation trends (record $2.3 trillion invested in 2025, solar PV nearing parity with coal-backed generation) support a resilient demand environment for solar manufacturers
- Order book stood at 8.2 GW as at 31 March 2026, providing visibility across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, and government segments with short- to medium-term execution timelines
- Highest-ever quarterly booking of 1.9 GW recorded in Q4 FY26
- Order book segment mix: IPP 69%, Government 13%, EPC 11%, C&I 7%
- Order book geographic mix: Domestic 87%, Exports 13%
- Cumulative global shipments of solar modules crossed 10 GW during the year, reinforcing customer confidence and market footprint
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Vikram Solar scaled module capacity to 9.5GW with full N-type transition and is advancing 12GW cell capacity at Gangaikondan, driving margin expansion through automation and pass-through pricing; the strategic shift toward vertical integration and export-ready supply chains positions it to capture India’s 50GW+ solar growth and global demand shifts post-China VAT rebate changes.
